subject.title: Feature: Graph-aware loop detection for sessions_send (triangular/polygonal cascades bypass maxPingPongTurns)

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed before `sessions_send` delivery when propagated inter-agent provenance shows the target agent already participated in the current route?
rationale: The source-level fix is bounded, but it intentionally changes existing cyclic multi-agent routes from delivered work into errors and the linked PR is draft/conflicting, so maintainer product and compatibility intent is required before landing.

options.title: Accept fail-closed cycle blocking
options.body: Land the linked provenance-chain guard after review, proof, and conflict cleanup so A -> B -> C -> A routes stop before a repeated agent run.

options.title: Preserve cyclic revisits
options.body: Reject or rework the guard if legitimate workflows must be able to revisit an agent in the same route without a tool error.

options.title: Require explicit route policy
options.body: Ask for an opt-in or thresholded route policy if maintainers want protection without changing revisit behavior by default.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed cycle blocking
recommendation.body: Land the linked provenance-chain guard after review, proof, and conflict cleanup so A -> B -> C -> A routes stop before a repeated agent run.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest observed history across inter-session provenance, session helper contracts, and `sessions_send` delivery boundaries points here.
